syscalls.comment: CyberCheck fetcher: deny kernel-module, mount, keyring, bpf, perf, ptrace, io_uring, clock, swap, reboot and similar syscalls. clone/clone3/unshare/setns stay allowed: Chromium's user-namespace sandbox needs them (Docker's default profile allows them only with CAP_SYS_ADMIN, which cap_drop ALL removes). Only the x86_64 ABI is listed: 32-bit (int 0x80 / socketcall) and x32 system calls are refused as a foreign architecture, so they cannot get around the socket() argument checks.

socket(): address families >= 17 (AF_PACKET, AF_RDS, AF_TIPC, AF_BLUETOOTH, AF_ALG, AF_VSOCK, AF_XDP, ...) fail with EAFNOSUPPORT. An unsigned 64-bit comparison, so a family with junk in the upper 32 bits (which the kernel truncates away) is denied too. Chromium, Node and Python use only AF_UNIX (1), AF_INET (2), AF_INET6 (10) and AF_NETLINK (16).

socket(): the obsolete families below 16 (AF_AX25, AF_IPX, AF_APPLETALK, AF_NETROM, AF_BRIDGE, AF_ATMPVC, AF_X25, AF_ROSE, AF_DECnet, AF_NETBEUI, AF_SECURITY, AF_KEY) fail with EAFNOSUPPORT. Several conditions on the same argument are OR-ed (one rule each); a value with upper bits set is already caught by the >= 17 rule.

socket(AF_NETLINK, *, NETLINK_NETFILTER (nf_tables)) fails with EPROTONOSUPPORT: with the user and network namespaces Chromium's sandbox needs, a process gets a namespaced CAP_NET_ADMIN, and this is a usual kernel privilege-escalation surface. Conditions on different arguments are AND-ed; the masks compare only the low 32 bits the kernel uses. NETLINK_ROUTE (0), which Chromium uses, stays allowed.
